trend: First Reddit post: introduce the founder and the brand to Indian founders and ask for feedback
why: Founder posts asking for honest feedback are welcome here. It gives SILT a credible first footprint on Reddit.
rules: Founder introductions asking for feedback are usually allowed. Don't post a store link or discount code in the post. Check the sidebar for a weekly promotion thread or the right flair, and say you're the founder.
title: I left 10+ years of corporate to build a two-drink wellness routine for busy professionals. We launched 3 weeks ago. Would love your honest feedback.
text:
Hi r/StartUpIndia, I'm Abhishek, founder of SILT Nutrition. Posting from my personal account, so full disclosure that this is my company.

The problem I kept living through in corporate was a 3 PM crash in the day and a mind that wouldn't switch off at night. The fix people suggested was always another jar, and I ended up with a shelf of supplements I couldn't stick to.

So we built two drink mixes in stick packs. Mornings has 80 mg caffeine with 200 mg L-theanine, 5 g fibre, probiotics, and D3, K2, B12 and C. Nights has 3 g glycine, 250 mg magnesium bisglycinate, 300 mg ashwagandha and 200 mg L-theanine. Every dose is printed on the pack, there are no proprietary blends, and we publish a lab report for each of the 19 ingredients (293 checks so far, none failed).

Where we are: 1,870 pre-bookings before launch, then 250 customers and 10 repeat orders in the first 15 days, and 4.9 out of 5 on verified reviews. Price works out to about ₹60 a day per drink.

What I'd really value from this sub:

1. Does ₹60 a day feel fair for a daily drink like this, or is that the wrong way to frame price?
2. We sell on our own site today. For a habit product, would you push into quick commerce early or wait?
3. Publishing lab reports has helped trust so far. What else would make you believe a new supplement brand?

Happy to answer anything, including the parts that aren't working yet.
